props.name: avoid sulphur and halides

evidence.quote: It is important, however, to avoid 10 the. presence of impurities or contaminatin substances which may have a deleterious ef. fect. Thus, it is desirable to avoid the pres- ence of sulphur, the halides, ete.

reved. catalysts described are halide-free, 105 they are simply and cheaply produced and are highly resistant in the sense that they are well adapted to retain for a long period.of | time, the proper qualities to serve as a cat- |

props.statement: Impurities with a deleterious effect must be avoided, in particular sulphur and the halides; the catalysts described are halide-free, simply and cheaply produced and retain their catalytic qualities for a long time.

props.name: more copper: more activity, shorter life

evidence.quote: the activity of the catalyst may be increased by lessening the atomic per cent of zinc and correspondingly 120 increasing that of copper. Thus 4 to 1,3 to 1, 2 to 1 and 1 to 1 ratios give larger yields at lower operating temperatures than'a 5 to 1 tatio.
On the other hand, the higher the copper percentage the shorter the life or 125 stability of the catalyst.

props.statement: Lessening the zinc and increasing the copper raises activity: 4:1, 3:1, 2:1 and 1:1 ratios give larger yields at lower temperatures than a 5:1 ratio; but the higher the copper percentage the shorter the life or stability, so a high zinc atomic per cent is desirable even at some loss in activity.

props.name: large excess of zinc; Zn:Cu at least 4:1 preferred

evidence.quote: The composition can be varied within quite wide limits. It seems quite important, how- ever, to employ a large excess of zinc. Pref- erably, the ratio of zinc to copper (atomic proportions) is at least four to one, but this may be reduced to two to one, or even lower, but. with less satisfactory results.

props.statement: The composition can be varied widely, but a large excess of zinc is important: preferably the zinc to copper atomic ratio is at least four to one; it may be reduced to two to one or lower with less satisfactory results.

props.statement: The ranges of speed, temperature and pressure known in the art are suitable; high pressures are preferred, while the temperatures need be only moderately high.

props.statement: Method of producing a stable highly active copper zinc oxide catalyst: reducing copper carbonate admixed with zinc carbonate, at least two atoms of zinc to one of copper, in a heated reducing gas, giving zinc oxide and stable purplish free copper.

props.name: alkali carbonate best; NaOH reasonably active; NH4OH decidedly less active

evidence.quote: Thus, the best re- sults are obtained by employing an alkali metal carbonate for precipitating the zinc and copper compounds.
owever, a reasonably active catalyst may ®& be obtained by precipitating from the ni-
It is also possible to use: ammonium hy- droxide to precipitate the metals from the _ solution: of soluble salts, but.a decidedly less active catalyst results.

props.statement: The best results are obtained by precipitating with an alkali metal carbonate; precipitation with sodium or potassium hydroxide gives a reasonably active catalyst, with ammonium hydroxide a decidedly less active one.

props.name: precipitation for purity and form; joint precipitation perhaps not essential

evidence.quote: The initial compounds of the improved catalyst are produced by precipitation of the compounds from solutions of the metals for two reasons. One is to insure purity; and another is to insure the desired form of the catalyst
The joint precipi- _ tation, while important from the standpoint of easy production of an intimately com- mingled mixture perhaps is not an abselute essential..

props.statement: The initial compounds are made by precipitation from solutions to insure purity and the desired form of the catalyst; joint precipitation gives an intimately commingled mixture but is perhaps not absolutely essential.

props.name: treated zinc oxide well structured; copper stable in air

evidence.quote: The zinc 85 — oxide possesses as a result of the treatment, a physical structure which is well adapted to— the purpose of the catalyst.
Copper produced by the method - described does. not.deteriovate if exposed to ~ ; air.

props.statement: After the treatment the zinc oxide has a physical structure well adapted to the purpose of the catalyst, and the copper produced does not deteriorate if exposed to air.

props.name: zinc oxide - copper mixtures as highly effective contact body

evidence.quote: it is possible to prepare mixtures of zine oxide and copper in such a state or condition that a highly effective contact body is afforded;
ex- a5 perience has shown that the physical. condi- tion of the materials in the mixture is a most important factor, as is also the composition of the materials employed.

props.statement: Mixtures of zinc oxide and copper can be prepared in a state giving a highly effective contact body for the reaction of carbon oxides and hydrogen; the physical condition as well as the composition of the materials is a most important factor.
